about.title: Norwalk Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Seven people died on Norwalk streets in 2025, according to public collision records. Behind each of those counts is a household that has to figure out the next morning. If that is where you are, a wrongful death claim is one of the few tools California offers to hold the responsible party accountable in civil court, apart from whatever happens in a criminal case. Norwalk's highest-volume corridors — Rosecrans Avenue, Imperial Highway, Pioneer Boulevard and Studebaker Road — show up most often in the city's 413 injury collisions, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. see the heaviest reported activity. Fatal cases also arise from unsafe premises, defective products and medical errors. State law gives spouses, domestic partners and children first standing to file, followed by certain dependents and heirs, and it sets a two-year deadline from the date of death, with a shorter window when a public agency is involved. We handle these cases on contingency, at no cost to you unless we recover.

items.title: Standing is sorted out early
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death action, starting with the spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. We can confirm who in your family is eligible before anything is filed.

items.title: The two-year clock is respected
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file in California, and the window shrinks considerably when a city, county or state agency may share fault. Reaching out sooner keeps those deadlines from closing quietly.

items.title: Every category of loss is accounted for
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on Imperial Highway. Does the criminal case decide our claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs separately from any criminal charges the Los Angeles County District Attorney may bring. The civil case uses a different standard of proof and can move forward whether or not a driver is prosecuted or convicted. We can also request the collision report and other records from that stretch of road.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children have the first right to bring the claim. If none exist, the law extends standing to certain dependents and heirs, such as parents who relied on the deceased for support. Because these rules can be specific, it helps to have us review your family's situation before filing.

items.question: How long do we have, and does it matter if a government agency was involved?
items.answer: California generally gives two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a public entity — a city, county or state agency — may be responsible, a formal claim must be presented much sooner, often within months. Reaching out early gives us time to identify every responsible party before any deadline passes.
